questions.question: What are the three main executables that come with Robot Framework installation? (Select all that apply)

options.text: robot - for executing suites
rebot - for post-processing execution results
libdoc - for generating keyword documentation
robotc - for compiling test suites
options.explanation: There is no robotc command; RF doesn't compile suites

options.text: rfrun - for running tests in parallel
options.explanation: There is no rfrun command in standard RF installation

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the 'robot' executable?

options.text: To execute suites and their containing tests or tasks
To generate keyword documentation for libraries
options.explanation: Documentation generation is done by libdoc, not robot

options.text: To post-process execution results and regenerate reports
options.explanation: Post-processing is done by rebot, not robot

options.text: To validate syntax without executing tests
options.explanation: While robot parses files, its primary purpose is execution

questions.question: What is the basic syntax to run the robot command?

options.text: robot <path_to_root_suite>
robot --execute <path_to_root_suite>
options.explanation: No --execute flag is needed; path is sufficient

options.text: robot run <path_to_root_suite>
options.explanation: No 'run' subcommand is needed

options.text: <path_to_root_suite> | robot
options.explanation: Robot expects the path as an argument, not via pipe

questions.question: Given a directory structure where 'robot_files' contains 'TestSuite.robot', and your current working directory contains the 'robot_files' directory, which command correctly executes the suite?

options.text: robot robot_files
robot robot_files/TestSuite.robot
options.explanation: While this works, the question asks for executing the directory

options.text: robot --suite robot_files
options.explanation: --suite is for filtering, not specifying the path

options.text: python robot robot_files
options.explanation: The robot command is directly executable

questions.question: Where should optional configuration options be placed in the robot command?

options.text: BEFORE the path to the suite file or directory
AFTER the path to the suite file or directory
options.explanation: Options must come before the path argument

options.text: In a separate configuration file only
options.explanation: Options can be passed directly on the command line before the path

options.text: Options are not supported by the robot command
options.explanation: Robot supports many configuration options

questions.question: Which of the following are valid robot command examples? (Select all that apply)

options.text: robot tests/
robot --loglevel DEBUG tests/
robot --variable VAR:value tests/
robot tests/ --outputdir results
options.explanation: Options must come BEFORE the path, not after

questions.question: How can you learn about available options for the robot command?

options.text: Run: robot --help
Run: robot --options
options.explanation: The correct flag is --help, not --options

options.text: Run: help robot
options.explanation: This is shell help, not robot's built-in help

options.text: Options are not documented in the command line
options.explanation: Robot provides comprehensive --help documentation

questions.question: What three output files does Robot Framework generate by default after executing a suite? (Select all that apply)

options.text: output.xml - machine-readable file with all logged execution details
log.html - detailed HTML log with keyword-level details
report.html - summary report with execution statistics
results.json - JSON format execution results
options.explanation: RF doesn't generate results.json by default

options.text: debug.log - debugging information file
options.explanation: There is no debug.log generated by default

questions.question: What is the relationship between output.xml, log.html, and report.html?

options.text: log.html and report.html are generated based on information in output.xml
output.xml is generated from log.html and report.html
options.explanation: It's the opposite - output.xml is the source

options.text: All three are generated independently
options.explanation: log.html and report.html are derived from output.xml

options.text: They all contain identical information in different formats
options.explanation: output.xml is comprehensive; log.html and report.html show different views

questions.question: Which file contains ALL logged execution details and is machine-readable?

options.text: output.xml
log.html
options.explanation: log.html is for humans, not machine processing

options.text: report.html
options.explanation: report.html is a summary, not comprehensive details

options.text: All three files contain the same information
options.explanation: output.xml is the most comprehensive source

questions.question: What unique feature does Robot Framework provide in its logging?

options.text: It logs each keyword call with arguments, outputs, and timestamps for detailed execution flow
It only logs failed keywords to save space
options.explanation: RF logs all keywords including passed and not-run ones

options.text: It generates video recordings of test execution
options.explanation: RF doesn't generate videos by default

options.text: It automatically sends logs to a central server
options.explanation: Log storage is local by default

questions.question: What information can you see in Robot Framework logs even for passed tests? (Select all that apply)

options.text: All passed keywords with their arguments
Non-executed keywords (in conditional branches not taken)
Timestamps for each keyword
Only failed keywords are logged
options.explanation: RF logs all keywords, not just failures

questions.question: What are the four status labels used by Robot Framework? (Select all that apply)

options.text: PASS
FAIL
SKIP
NOT RUN
ERROR
options.explanation: ERROR is a log level, not a status label

options.text: PENDING
options.explanation: PENDING is not a Robot Framework status label

questions.question: Which status labels can be applied to suites, test cases, tasks, AND keywords? (Select all that apply)

options.text: PASS
FAIL
SKIP
NOT RUN
options.explanation: NOT RUN is an additional status specifically for keywords

questions.question: What is the NOT RUN status used for?

options.text: Keywords that were not executed during execution due to failures or conditions
Tests that were skipped by tagging
options.explanation: Skipped tests use SKIP status, not NOT RUN

options.text: Suites that were excluded from execution
options.explanation: NOT RUN is specifically for keywords, not suites

options.text: Tests that haven't been written yet
options.explanation: NOT RUN refers to runtime execution, not test completion

questions.question: What is the difference between atomic and composite elements in terms of status determination?

options.text: Atomic elements define their own status; composite elements base their status on child elements
Atomic elements don't have status; only composite elements do
options.explanation: Both have status, but determine it differently

options.text: Composite elements always PASS if any child passes
options.explanation: Composite elements need all executed children to PASS

options.text: There is no difference in status determination
options.explanation: The determination method differs significantly

questions.question: When is an atomic element (like a Library Keyword) marked as PASS?

options.text: When it was executed successfully without reporting an error by raising an exception
When it was not executed at all
options.explanation: Non-executed keywords are NOT RUN, not PASS

options.text: When it raised an expected exception
options.explanation: This describes specific keywords like 'Run Keyword And Expect Error', not general atomic elements

options.text: When at least one of its child keywords passed
options.explanation: Atomic elements don't have child keywords

questions.question: When is a composite element (like a User Keyword or test case) marked as PASS?

options.text: When all directly executed body elements are PASS
When at least one body element is PASS
options.explanation: All executed elements must PASS, not just one

options.text: When it has no FAIL elements, including NOT RUN
options.explanation: NOT RUN elements don't affect PASS status; only executed elements matter

options.text: When the first keyword is PASS
options.explanation: All executed keywords must PASS, not just the first

questions.question: Consider a User Keyword that calls three Library Keywords. The first two PASS, the third FAILS. What is the User Keyword's status?

options.text: FAIL - because one of its directly called keywords failed
PASS - because majority of keywords passed
options.explanation: All executed keywords must PASS; one FAIL makes the whole keyword FAIL

options.text: SKIP - because it didn't complete successfully
options.explanation: Failures result in FAIL, not SKIP

options.text: NOT RUN - because it couldn't finish
options.explanation: NOT RUN is for keywords not executed; this keyword was executed

questions.question: How does the 'Run Keyword And Expect Error' keyword from BuiltIn Library determine its PASS status?

options.text: It PASSES if the keyword it internally calls raises an error with the expected message or type
It PASSES only if the internal keyword succeeds without errors
options.explanation: This keyword expects an error, so it PASSES when error occurs

options.text: It always FAILS because it contains a failing keyword
options.explanation: Expected failures are PASS for this keyword

options.text: It SKIPS if the internal keyword fails
options.explanation: Expected failures result in PASS, not SKIP

questions.question: Can a composite element (suite, test, or User Keyword) be PASS even if some of its deeper child elements are FAIL?

options.text: Yes, if the FAIL is within a keyword like 'Run Keyword And Expect Error' that expects the failure
No, any FAIL at any level always propagates to the top
options.explanation: Expected failures (like in 'Run Keyword And Expect Error') don't propagate

options.text: Yes, failures are never propagated upward
options.explanation: Unexpected failures do propagate upward

options.text: Only suites can be PASS with child failures
options.explanation: Any composite element can be PASS if child failures are expected

questions.question: When is an atomic element marked as FAIL?

options.text: When it was tried to be executed but raised an exception
When it was not executed at all
options.explanation: Non-executed keywords are NOT RUN, not FAIL

options.text: When it returned a false value
options.explanation: Return values don't determine FAIL; exceptions do

options.text: When it took longer than expected
options.explanation: Timeout causes exception which leads to FAIL, but timing alone doesn't

questions.question: When is a composite element marked as FAIL?

options.text: When at least one of its directly executed body elements is FAIL
When all of its body elements are FAIL
options.explanation: Only one FAIL is needed to make the composite FAIL

options.text: When it has any NOT RUN elements
options.explanation: NOT RUN elements don't cause FAIL status

options.text: When it was not executed at all
options.explanation: Non-executed elements would be SKIP or NOT RUN

questions.question: What typically happens to subsequent keywords when a failure occurs?

options.text: They are skipped, with exceptions like Teardowns
They continue executing normally
options.explanation: By default, keywords after a failure are skipped

options.text: They are marked as FAIL without execution
options.explanation: Non-executed keywords are marked as NOT RUN, not FAIL

options.text: The entire suite stops immediately
options.explanation: Typically the test stops, but the suite continues with next tests

questions.question:
Analyze this test execution scenario:

```
Test Case: Login Test
  1. Open Browser        → PASS
  2. Input Username      → PASS
  3. Input Password      → FAIL
  4. Click Login         → NOT RUN
  5. Verify Dashboard    → NOT RUN
```

What is the status of the test case?

options.text: FAIL - because keyword 3 failed
PASS - because 2 out of 5 keywords passed
options.explanation: One failure makes the entire test FAIL

options.text: NOT RUN - because keywords 4 and 5 didn't run
options.explanation: The test was executed (not NOT RUN); it just failed

options.text: SKIP - because it didn't complete
options.explanation: Incomplete due to failure is FAIL, not SKIP

questions.question: How does failure typically propagate through the hierarchy?

options.text: Upwards: failed Library Keyword → failed User Keyword → failed test → failed suite
Downwards: failed suite → failed test → failed keywords
options.explanation: Failures originate from keywords and propagate up

options.text: Failures don't propagate; each level is independent
options.explanation: Failures do propagate upward through the hierarchy

options.text: Horizontally: failed test affects sibling tests
options.explanation: Failures don't affect sibling tests by default

questions.question: What are the two kinds of logging information in Robot Framework?

options.text: Console Output - printed to terminal during execution
Log Messages - written to output.xml and log.html
Debug Files - separate debugging information
options.explanation: There are no separate debug files; debug info goes into log messages

options.text: Audit Logs - for compliance tracking
options.explanation: There is no separate audit log mechanism

questions.question: What is the key difference between Console Output and Log Messages?

options.text: Console Output is typically not persistent; Log Messages are persistent in output.xml
Console Output is more detailed than Log Messages
options.explanation: Log Messages are typically more detailed

options.text: Log Messages appear during execution; Console Output appears after
options.explanation: It's the opposite - Console Output appears during execution

options.text: They contain identical information
options.explanation: They serve different purposes and contain different information

questions.question: What severity levels can Log Messages have? (Select all that apply)

options.text: INFO
DEBUG
TRACE
WARN
ERROR
CRITICAL
options.explanation: CRITICAL is not a standard RF log level

options.text: Both test cases passed
The suite 'TestSuite' passed
Total of 2 tests were executed
Zero tests failed
Which specific keywords were executed
options.explanation: Keyword details are in log.html, not in this summary output
